comment: Increment-3 mutation ledger. Each entry names a module, a unique source substring and its replacement, the wave that introduced it, and the verdict of the last sweep. The set is checked in so the next sweep is a re-run rather than a re-invention, and so a shrinking survivor list is visible in a diff (increment-2 review, mutation-methodology adjudication, amendment 2). Wave 1 (152) was designed before this increment's survivor-killing tests existed. Wave 2 (79) was designed afterwards, deliberately over anchors wave 1 never touched -- a set chosen to be killed is not evidence, a set chosen to reach untouched code is. Wave 2 carries one declared CONTROL ARM (W-M11-CONTROL), a semantic no-op that MUST survive: if the sweep reports it killed, the harness is not reporting verdicts that come from the mutation and every other verdict in that run is worthless. Run with mut/sweep.py in the tester's scratchpad; the oracle is the whole suite with -x, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, __pycache__ purged around every mutation, and the original text rewritten in the finally. Do not run two sweeps concurrently: the increment-3 tester observed one spurious 'killed' (W-J01, 3.12) from CPU contention against the suite's performance pins, which UNDER-reports survivors. WAVE 3 (increment-3 review, 59 mutants): designed over anchors NEITHER prior wave touched -- cost/source.py's snapshot validators, detect/base.py's Finding validators and helpers, detect/registry.py's waste mapping, report/json_out.py's timestamp and identifier boundary, and every line the review's own fix commits added. 54 killed, 5 survived: 2 equivalent, 3 real gaps now closed. Two of the three real gaps were in code the review itself had just written, which is the argument for sweeping a fix and not only the thing it fixed. HARNESS: also verify a tree digest between mutants -- a sweep killed mid-mutation leaves a mutated baseline and the next run reports against it. A mutation whose subject was deleted carries retired: true and is skipped by a sweep; it stays in the file because the finding is the point, not the anchor. HARNESS CONTRACT, added by the increment-3 review after breaking its own sweep: do NOT put a test in the suite that compares a ledger anchor to its module's source text. 44 anchors here are shared by two or more entries and 18 more are nested inside another's, so applying any mutation makes its siblings match neither form -- such a test fails for every mutant and the sweep reports 100% killed, control arm included. Observed: one full run reported 289/289 killed for exactly this reason, and the control arm was the only signal. The anchor check belongs in the harness, which reports NOT-APPLIED.
operators: guard-clause drop: `if X and Y` -> `if X`; `if X` -> `if False`
negation drop or insertion: `not X` -> `X`, `is None` -> `is not None`
normalization drop: sorted(), set(), tuple(), dict()
rung / branch reorder (R27 ladder, R30 priority order)
literal substitution (string constants, rounding modes, quanta)
control-flow swap: continue <-> break, early return removal

mutations.regression_note: increment-3 review: this mutant went from KILLED to SURVIVING as a side effect of the review's own BUG-1 fix, and was caught only by re-running the whole checked-in ledger against the fixed tree. Moving quantize_cost inside the guard made InvalidOperation and Inexact indistinguishable for every input the suite drove, so R29's central clause became unfalsifiable. Killed again by test_r29_inexact_is_trapped_and_not_only_invalid_operation. This is the argument for amendment 4 (run the checked-in sweep in CI): a fix can silently disarm a check, and nothing but a re-run says so.

mutations.why_it_survives: RETIRED, not killed. This mutant narrowed `except (OSError, ValueError)` to `except OSError` in cli/main.expand_inputs. The clause is deleted, so the anchor no longer exists and the mutant has no subject.
